question: ap1
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out with a total budget under $20,000. Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Primed-versus-naive re-stimulation time course with ATAC/CUT&RUN
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) with a transient signal such as TNF, EGF or PMA, rest them for days to weeks, then restimulate and compare to naive cells. Measure chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding by CUT&RUN, H3K27ac, and nascent transcription (PRO-seq/4sU-seq) to see whether AP-1-bound sites stay open and give faster or stronger responses (cost roughly $8–12k).

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the rest phase
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin-degron or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either only during the initial stimulus or only during the rest period, then restimulate. If memory needs continuous AP-1 occupancy, depletion during rest will erase the primed response. If AP-1 is only needed to establish memory, depletion during rest will not erase it, which separates initiation from maintenance (about $10–15k with existing degron lines or CRISPR knock-in).

ideas.title: Site-specific AP-1 motif perturbation and reporter test
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate or delete AP-1 motifs, or use dCas9-KRAB/dCas9 blocking, at a few primed enhancers. Test whether memory of accessibility and of gene induction is lost. In parallel, run a lentiviral MPRA or reporter library with wild-type and mutated AP-1 motifs, integrated and chromatinized, to test sufficiency and motif-grammar rules (about $6–10k).

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and live-cell imaging of heritability
ideas.description: Run 10x multiome (RNA + ATAC) on stimulated, rested and restimulated cells to link AP-1 motif activity (chromVAR) to single-cell memory states. Add a live-cell AP-1 reporter (e.g., a FOS-promoter or AP-1 response element driving destabilized fluorescent protein) and track lineages by time-lapse across divisions to measure how long the state lasts and whether sister cells inherit it, which would indicate bistable or self-sustaining memory (about $12–18k).

ideas.title: Reanalysis of public datasets for AP-1 memory signatures
ideas.description: Mine existing ATAC, ChIP and RNA-seq data from trained immunity, wound-healing, neuronal activity, and epithelial inflammatory-memory studies. Test whether sites that stay open after stimulus withdrawal are enriched for AP-1 motifs and binding, and whether this predicts faster re-induction. Check for co-occurrence with pioneer factors (e.g., CEBP, ETS) and for histone mark persistence, which gives cheap, cross-system evidence of generality (under $2k compute).
